\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بیزار} (bezār)}{بیزار (bezār)}]{\ur{بیزار} (bezār) — fed up; weary (of something)}

\label{lesson:UR-C448-bezar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for consolation, then the Urdu for pleasant.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بیزار}}
\textbf{\ur{بیزار}} — \emph{bezār} — \textquotedblleft{}fed up; weary (of something)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{وہ} \ur{روز} \ur{ایک} \ur{ہی} \ur{کام} \ur{سے} \ur{بیزار} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{voh roz ek hī kām se bezār hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He is fed up with doing the same work every day.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بیزار}} (\emph{bezār}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{bēzār}, \textquotedblleft{}weary of, sick of\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bezār}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bezār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{voh roz ek hī kām se bezār hai.} — He is fed up with doing the same work every day.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for consolation, then the Urdu for pleasant, then say \emph{bezār} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{بیزار} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Fed up; weary (of something)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{تجسس} (tajassus)}{تجسس (tajassus)}]{\ur{تجسس} (tajassus) — curiosity}

\label{lesson:UR-C448-tajassus}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for fed up, then the Urdu for interesting.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{تجسس}}
\textbf{\ur{تجسس}} — \emph{tajassus} — \textquotedblleft{}curiosity\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بچے} \ur{کی} \ur{آنکھوں} \ur{میں} \ur{تجسس} \ur{تھا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bachche kī āṅkhoṅ meṅ tajassus thā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There was curiosity in the child's eyes.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{تجسس}} (\emph{tajassus}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{tajassus}, \textquotedblleft{}prying\textquotedblright{}; Urdu uses it for plain curiosity.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bachche kī āṅkhoṅ meṅ tajassus thā.} — There was curiosity in the child's eyes.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for fed up, then the Urdu for interesting, then say \emph{tajassus} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بیتاب} (betāb)}{بیتاب (betāb)}]{\ur{بیتاب} (betāb) — eager; impatient}

\label{lesson:UR-C448-betab}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for interesting, then the Urdu for curiosity.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بیتاب}}
\textbf{\ur{بیتاب}} — \emph{betāb} — \textquotedblleft{}eager; impatient\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بچے} \ur{چھٹی} \ur{کے} \ur{لیے} \ur{بیتاب} \ur{ہیں۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bachche chhuṭṭī ke liye betāb haiṅ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The children can't wait for the holiday.
\end{quote}

\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ٹوہنا} (ṭohnā)}{ٹوہنا (ṭohnā)}]{\ur{ٹوہنا} (ṭohnā) — to feel about for; to probe}

\label{lesson:UR-C448-tohna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for curiosity, then the Urdu for eager.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ٹوہنا}}
\textbf{\ur{ٹوہنا}} — \emph{ṭohnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to feel about for; to probe\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{جیب} \ur{میں} \ur{چابی} \ur{ٹوہی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{us ne jeb meṅ chābī ṭohī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He felt about in his pocket for the key.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{دیوار} \ur{ٹوہی}, \emph{us ne dīvār ṭohī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ٹوہنا}} (\emph{ṭohnā}) is inherited from \emph{ṭōh}, \textquotedblleft{}grope\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs (CDIAL 5486).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭohnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{us ne jeb meṅ chābī ṭohī.} — He felt about in his pocket for the key.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for curiosity, then the Urdu for eager, then say \emph{ṭohnā} again
\end{itemize}
